scope: Targeted parent semantic checks of decisive memory contributions against available originals. All 16 outputs read separately; this is not an exhaustive accuracy estimate.

checks.claim: Ibn Kathir explicitly moves from physical animal travel to spiritual/religious paths at 16:9
TDV 38:32–33 chooses forgetting remembrance and striking the horses, unlike DIB
checks.finding: The official TDV text and DUZ copy say love for remembrance and stroking; QE also retains the positive love clause. This does not establish what every historical edition said, but contradicts the named available copies.

checks.claim: Ibn Kathir explicitly relates physical roads to spiritual/religious paths at 16:9
Qualified Asha attribution كند لوصل الزائر المعتاد
checks.finding: Not located in the four available poetry works; the named Asha Diwan is not part of the assigned corpus. A no-match search does not establish falsity.

checks.claim: TDV 38:32 chooses love over remembrance, in contrast to DIB
checks.finding: Same positive remembrance choice in available TDV copies. Max did not fix the high attribution error. Max does not repeat high’s striking claim; its error is the motive clause.

checks.claim: Koytak–Erturk Turkish Asad 16:8 uses the future yaratacak
checks.anchor: O, bilmediğiniz daha neler neler yaratmaktadır
checks.finding: English Asad will yet create is accurate; the available named Turkish witness has yaratmaktadır, not yaratacak. The memory comparison misattributes a tense.

checks.claim: Asad 18:28 makes following one’s own desires an explicit cause of heedlessness
anchors: because he had always followed [only] his own desires

checks.claim: Wahidi links 2:194 to Hudaybiyya and the following year’s umra
checks.anchor: فلما كان العام المقبل دخلوا مكة، فاعتمروا في ذي القعدة
checks.finding: A relevant available source not extracted by either corpus Sol historical agent. The source’s explicit adjacent 2:194 section is missed by the verse index; keyword discovery finds it.
